subject: Private deployment evidence & key custody options
messages:
From: Julia Reed <compliance@medtechsolutions.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment questions — evidence & transfers

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick intro (Arjun looped me in). We're evaluating Redwood for a private on-prem deployment and need to gather the compliance pack to present to our legal team. Can you please provide the following as soon as possible?

- Current DPA template and any suggested customer-facing redline language for customer-managed keys (we need explicit clauses about key custody and emergency break-glass).
- Full list of subprocessors (name, role, country) and which subprocessors, if any, have access to telemetry or operator consoles.
- A short operator-access matrix: what level of access Redwood engineers will have for on-prem vs VPC private control plane, and what logs/telemetry are available to customers.
- Confirmation on cross-border transfers: if our data stays in EU on an on-prem setup, do you still require any backup replication to non-EU regions?
- Evidence artifacts we can attach to our SOC2/ISO review (SOC2 report, network diagram, deployment runbook stub).

We also need a high-level network diagram to include in our security assessment. If there's a standard bundle you provide for private deployments, please send it.

Best,
Julia Reed
Head of Compliance
MedTech Solutions

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Hi Julia — thanks for the list, and welcome Arjun. Quick note from our side: we can absolutely support an on-prem private deployment with customer-controlled keys and provide the artifacts you requested. I've looped in Marcus for the subprocessor and architecture details and Mina from Security for the SOC2/controls evidence and operator access matrix.

Planned next steps:
- Marcus will attach the current subprocessor register and a sanitized architecture diagram we use for procurement packs.
- Mina will confirm what telemetry/logging we expose to customers and how operator access is scoped for on-prem vs private VPC control plane.
- I'll send a DPA template with suggested redline language for key custody and an initial answer on cross-border replication. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call with legal + security next week to walk through the items.

If you have any timing constraints for your review, let me know and we'll prioritize.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks

Julia — attaching the two artifacts we often share early in a procurement review. Please consider the subprocessor register as the current snapshot; we update quarterly and can provide a signed attestation for procurement if needed.

Attachments (stubs):
- subprocessor_list_2026.csv (csv) — columns: name, purpose, country, access_level
- onprem_architecture.png (png) — sanitized network diagram for private/on-prem deployments

A few clarifications inline:
- Customer-managed keys: for on-prem we support HSM-backed key material that customers control; Redwood operators do not hold the key material. For VPC/private control-plane deployments we support cloud KMS where customers can grant Redwood an envelope-wrapping role; we can provide standard clause text for either model.
- Operator access: for on-prem installs operator-run support is through a short-lived bastion connection initiated by the customer and logged; we do not provision long-term operator accounts. For private control plane (hosted control plane in customer VPC) there's a least-privilege operator role and we can provide the operator access runbook under NDA.
- Cross-border replication: by default, backups/replicas are colocated in the region you select for private deployments. We do not replicate on-prem customer data to Redwood-hosted regions unless a customer explicitly opts into managed DR that includes cross-region replication.

I'm happy to jump on a call to step through the diagram.

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Julia Reed <compliance@medtechsolutions.com>

Date: 2026-08-17T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — evidence & transfers

Thanks Marcus — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups after reviewing the subprocessor snapshot: 

- Can you provide the specific contract clause language you recommend for the DPA around the HSM/key custody (we'd like to pre-populate our redline). For example, language that states: "Redwood shall not access customer key material except under emergency break-glass procedures requested by the customer and logged to the customer's audit collector." Do you have a standard phrasing?
- Logging: we need confirmation that operator sessions will be logged and that session recordings / commands can be exported to our SIEM. If operator access is short-lived bastion-only, what logs are generated and how long are they retained?
- Evidence: can you attach your most recent SOC2 Type II report or provide an access path to view it under NDA?
- EU question: MedTech maintains all PHI/PII within EU boundaries. You mentioned backups are colocated, but if a managed DR option is chosen in the future would Redwood require data egress out of EU for recovery? We need an explicit statement on that so we can assess data residency risk.

If helpful, we can redact a few clauses on our side and share a suggested DPA redline; but we'd prefer to start from Redwood's recommended text.

Best,
Julia

Julia — quick update and concrete next steps from our side.

1) DPA and suggested clause language: attached is our standard DPA template (redacted for initial review) and an example paragraph you can drop into your redline for HSM/key custody. The key points: Redwood will not retain unencrypted key material for customer-managed HSMs; emergency access requires a customer-issued break-glass token and is recorded to the customer audit endpoint.

Attachment (stub): DPA_template_redwood_v3.pdf

Suggested clause excerpt (plain text):
"Customer retains sole possession and control of cryptographic key material used to encrypt Customer Data when Customer elects on-prem HSM custody. Redwood personnel shall not access unencrypted key material except when Customer provides a time-limited break-glass authorization. All break-glass events shall be logged and delivered to Customer's audit endpoint within 24 hours."

2) SOC2/controls: Mina will share the SOC2 access process under NDA; we can provide either a redacted report or a secure view link once an NDA is in place.

3) Operator access and logging: short-lived bastion sessions produce session logs and command telemetry; we can stream those logs to your SIEM (recommended) and retain an audit trail for 90 days by default (we can negotiate retention in the DPA).

4) EU residency: to be explicit — for pure on-prem installations where Customer elects to keep all network and storage on-prem within EU boundaries, Redwood will not, by default, replicate that on-prem customer data outside the EU. Any managed DR option that would involve cross-border replication would be subject to explicit customer authorization and contractual terms.

5) Next steps:
- I'll send a DocuSign envelope with the DPA template and an NDA link so Mina can provide SOC2 access.
- Marcus will prepare the operator access runbook excerpt (redacted).
- If you'd like a 30-minute call, available slots are Aug 20 9:00–11:00 or Aug 21 14:00–16:00 CET.
